event_var.var_meaning: overall survival status (Alive = alive at last follow-up, Dead = deceased)

notes: Provenance: variable names and values taken from the provided supplementary CSV header and rows (user-supplied data).

The paper (Yoon et al., npj Precision Oncology 2021) reports survival analyses (Kaplan–Meier) and states clinical information collected included postoperative survival; the CSV provides OS (month) numeric values.

Time origin is not explicitly stated in the CSV; the Methods state clinical information (postoperative tumor recurrence, survival) were collected, so OS time is likely months since surgery/postoperative, but this is not explicitly specified in the supplementary CSV and thus the exact time origin is 'unknown'.
Censoring convention is not explicitly described in the CSV; inferred convention: 'Alive' indicates a censored observation and 'Dead' indicates an event (death) for OS analyses.
Some other clinical fields in the CSV contain 'NA' values for other variables, but OS (month) and Vital status are present for the cohort used in analyses.

event_var.var_meaning: disease-free status at last follow-up (Yes = no recorded recurrence/metastasis during follow-up; No = recurrence and/or metastasis occurred)

notes: Provenance: variable names and values taken from the provided supplementary CSV header and rows (user-supplied data).
The paper explicitly reports disease-free survival (DFS) analyses (e.g., Kaplan–Meier DFS estimates) and uses DFS as an endpoint; the CSV contains 'Disease-free' (Yes/No) and numeric 'DFS (month)'.

From the CSV patterns (examples where 'No' corresponds to a shorter DFS (month) prior to later death), the 'Disease-free' field appears to mark whether a relapse/metastasis event occurred during follow-up; thus in survival terms 'No' corresponds to the occurrence of the DFS event (relapse).

Time origin for DFS (month) is not explicitly stated in the CSV; Methods indicate clinical data were postoperative, so DFS time is likely months from surgery/postoperative sampling but the exact origin is 'unknown'.
Censoring convention is not explicitly described in the CSV; inferred convention: 'Yes' indicates censored (no relapse observed), 'No' indicates event (relapse/metastasis).
